tagline: South down the Valley of the Moon, past Jack London's ranch.
intro: Out of the east side of Santa Rosa, Highway 12 turns south into the Sonoma Valley as the Sonoma Highway. It runs past Kenwood, with Bennett Mountain to the west and Sugarloaf Ridge off to the northeast, then down by Glen Ellen, where Sonoma Creek comes through, toward Agua Caliente and the town of Sonoma.

The Valley of the Moon is a translation of the name the Pomo and Coast Miwok peoples gave the valley. Jack London used it for the title of a novel, and lived at Glen Ellen from 1909 until his death in 1916.

moments.title: Kenwood
moments.text: The town tried on Rohrerville and Los Guilicos before a vote around 1895 settled on Kenwood, after people complained that Guilicos was hard to pronounce.

moments.title: Glen Ellen
moments.text: The town took its name from the vineyard Charles V. Stuart planted here and named Glen Ellen after his wife.

moments.title: Jack London State Historic Park
moments.text: On the slope of Sonoma Mountain stand the stone ruins of Wolf House, which burned in August 1913, before the Londons ever got to move in.
